gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-012 identifies the same ill-defined graph-space interface: the stated normal trace is only H^{-1/2}-valued while the definition and contradiction argument require an L2 flux norm. Its specific repair replaces that mismatch with an H^{-1/2} graph norm and duality. This recognizes the full substantive domain/norm incompatibility, though it presents the failure through the norm and sequence rather than explicitly restating every domain application.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The normal-trace construction is not well-defined with the stated H^{-1/2} trace domain and an L2 membership/norm requirement; the graph-space interface and subsequent Friedrichs argument must use H^{-1/2} consistently.
gold_decisions.uncovered_gold_detail: No substantive gold concern is left unrecognised; the prediction demonstrates the same defect through the incompatible flux norm and its corrected graph-space repair.

component_coverage.gold_component: The DefH1Gamma construction applies a merely H^{-1/2}-valued normal trace while requiring an L2 trace/norm, so the claimed set and Hilbert structure are undefined.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly states that the defined space guarantees only an H^{-1/2} normal trace, that the asserted L2 flux norm need not be finite, that the resulting contradiction sequence cannot be obtained in L2, and that the repair must use H^{-1/2} graph norms and duality.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both entries identify that dominated convergence for fixed g and h establishes only scalar or weak continuity, not the required operator-norm continuity or operator-norm limit, because no uniform control over all modes or unit-ball inputs is proved.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Pointwise or fixed-input convergence is insufficient for continuity in the bounded-operator norm; a uniform large-mode/tail estimate is required.

component_coverage.gold_component: The proof establishes only fixed-input scalar-pairing continuity and lacks the uniform unit-ball estimate needed for operator-norm continuity, including at zero.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-010 states exactly that dominated convergence fixes g and h, does not control the operator norm, and requires a uniform large-order estimate plus finite-mode/tail splitting.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold bundles two independently diagnosable failures in the Friedrichs contradiction proof: treating a parameter-indexed union as a Hilbert space and using unjustified L2 boundary convergence instead of H^{-1/2} convergence. ISSUE-013 independently diagnoses the non-vector-space and weak-limit failure, while ISSUE-012 independently diagnoses the incompatible L2/H^{-1/2} sequence and supplies the correct duality repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The wavenumber-uniform Friedrichs proof cannot pass to the claimed weak limit using the stated parameter-indexed union and L2 flux convergence; both the ambient compactness setting and the trace topology are invalid.
gold_decisions.uncovered_gold_detail: No substantive gold concern is left unrecognised; the two predictions separately diagnose the bundled space/compactness defect and the trace-topology/sequence defect.
gold_decisions.combination_explanation: The gold entry contains two distinct substantive defects: (1) the union of boundary-condition kernels over varying parameters is not generally a vector space or weakly closed, diagnosed self-containedly by ISSUE-013; and (2) failure of the H^{-1/2} estimate yields only H^{-1/2} convergence, not the L2 convergence assumed in the proof, diagnosed self-containedly by ISSUE-012. Together they cover the full invalid compactness and limit-passage argument.

component_coverage.gold_component: The union over all wavenumbers is incorrectly treated as a Hilbert space, so weak compactness and membership of the limit are unjustified.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-013 explicitly identifies the set as a union of parameter-indexed kernels that is not generally linear or Hilbert, explains why continuity does not ensure weak-limit membership, and repairs the proof by taking compactness in ambient H1.

component_coverage.gold_component: The contradiction argument replaces required H^{-1/2} trace convergence by L2 convergence and therefore cannot justify the boundary pairing or limit passage.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-012 states that the graph space supplies only an H^{-1/2} trace, that failure of the estimate yields only H^{-1/2} convergence rather than L2 convergence, and that the repair must use H^{-1/2}-H^{1/2} duality.
